objectives: Identify P, i, and n for a loan.

objectives: Build the first rows of an amortization schedule.

notes.body: Interest = balance × i (round to cents); principal = payment − interest; new balance = balance − principal.

questions.prompt: Grace drives about 10,000 miles per year and plans to keep a car 5 years. Gas costs $3.75 per gallon. Compare total cost of ownership.

parts.prompt: Find each loan payment and total of payments.
Find 5-year fuel, insurance, and maintenance costs for each.
Compute 5-year total cost of ownership (subtract resale value).
Recommend a car. What assumption is most uncertain?
parts.answer: Answers vary; resale value, repair costs, and gas prices are uncertain.

solutionSteps: TCO = down + total of payments + 5 × (insurance + maintenance) + fuel − resale.
questions.modelResponse: Over five years the Used sedan costs less ($27,382.72 vs $31,682.51). The hybrid’s fuel savings and lower APR offset part of its higher price, and it keeps more resale value; the used sedan risks larger repairs. Gas prices and resale values are the most uncertain assumptions, so I would rerun the numbers with higher and lower gas prices before deciding.
